about.title: El Cerrito Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: El Cerrito's mix of commuter traffic on I-80 and local movement along San Pablo Avenue, Route 123, and Potrero Avenue creates plenty of opportunity for collisions, and the most recent full year on record shows 52 injury crashes and 63 people hurt within the city. Wednesday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. see a noticeable rise in reported crashes, which lines up with the after-work rush through this part of Contra Costa County. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, what happens in the days right after matters. Photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage can disappear or get forgotten quickly, and insurance adjusters often reach out fast hoping to get a recorded statement before you've spoken with anyone else. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in the area who can review your situation and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cerrito Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Clock Doesn't Wait
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect on a route like Potrero Avenue was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for a crash near I-80 or on San Pablo Avenue. Your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Actually Lost
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover. That structure lets you focus on healing instead of legal bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, and once you've said something on record, it's hard to walk back. Speaking with an independent attorney first, before any recorded statement, protects your position.

items.question: What if my crash happened at a busy time like Wednesday afternoon on San Pablo Avenue?
items.answer: Rush-hour crashes often involve multiple vehicles and conflicting accounts, which makes early evidence — dashcam footage, witness names, traffic camera data — especially valuable. An attorney can help track that information down before it disappears. Timing alone doesn't change your legal rights, but it can affect how complicated the claim becomes.

items.question: Is there really no cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't charge anything to match you with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
